summary: An informational memo describing procedures for a graceful move from an ATMARP-based Logical IP Subnet to an NHRP-based network model over ATM.

eli5.summary: A guide for moving from an old way of finding addresses to a newer one without breaking the network along the way.

questions: how to migrate classical ip over atm to nhrp
subtitle: Moving from ATMARP to NHRP address resolution over ATM networks.

tldr.problem: Networks using ATMARP for address resolution over ATM need to migrate to NHRP, but both protocols must coexist during the transition to avoid breaking existing systems.
tldr.mechanism: NHRP servers are configured to respond to ATMARP client requests with the same answers they would give using NHRP, allowing ATMARP clients to function while NHRP clients gradually take over.
tldr.outcome: This allows a smooth migration from the older ATMARP approach to the newer NHRP model without requiring simultaneous cutover of all systems.

today: RFC 2336 is an Informational RFC that remains unobsoleted. It documents procedures for a specific transition period that was relevant in the late 1990s as ATM networks evolved.

sections.title: ATMARP to NHRP Migration
sections.content: This RFC addresses the practical problem of upgrading address resolution protocols in ATM networks. ATMARP (Classical IP and ARP over ATM) was an initial approach to running IP and address resolution over ATM Logical IP Subnets (LIS). NHRP (NBMA Next Hop Resolution Protocol) is a more capable replacement that determines both the internetworking layer address and the NBMA address of next hops toward a destination.
sections.eli5: ATMARP was the first way to look up addresses on ATM networks. NHRP is the better, newer way. This document is about switching from the old one to the new one without breaking anything.

sections.title: Server Compatibility Requirements
sections.content: During transition, both ATMARP clients and NHRP clients may exist on the same LIS. NHRP servers must be capable of responding to ATMARP client requests in the same manner as a traditional ATMARP server would. The server recognizes ATMARP packets by their LLC/SNAP code point and responds to specific operation codes. When an ATMARP request creates a cache entry on the NHRP server, that entry is marked as 'ATMARP' to distinguish it from entries created by NHRP clients.
sections.eli5: The new address book (NHRP server) learns to understand requests written in the old language (ATMARP) so old computers can still find addresses.

sections.title: Restrictions and Coexistence Rules
sections.content: The transition rules restrict NHRP servers to handling only SVC (Switched Virtual Circuit) based ATM connections, not PVC (Permanent Virtual Circuit) environments. A crucial restriction prevents NHRP servers from sending positive replies to NHRP requests seeking a station that registered via ATMARP if the requesting station is outside the target station's LIS, since ATMARP-registered stations typically cannot accept cut-through connections. Cache entries from ATMARP requests use a default holding time of 20 minutes.
sections.eli5: The new system knows not to promise direct connections for old-style registered computers if the request comes from far away, because those old computers are not ready for it.
